overview: Rapid review, October to early December 2026, of strategies to reduce low-value preoperative testing in adults having low-risk ambulatory or elective surgery, organised by strategy type, with durability and balancing outcomes and certainty rated per outcome.
population: Studies of adults having low-risk ambulatory or elective surgery in which routine preoperative tests (electrocardiogram, chest radiograph, blood count, coagulation, biochemistry) are advised against by local or national guidance.
exposure: Any strategy to reduce low-value testing: ordering system changes (order sets, defaults, decision support), feedback on clinicians' own ordering, pre-anaesthesia clinic triage, clinician education, patient-facing materials, or combinations.
procedures: The librarian searches three databases and a trial register from 2010, in English, building on the 2021 review's strategy. One analyst screens titles and abstracts; the second screens a random 20 percent and all exclusions at full text. One analyst extracts with a piloted form and the second checks all outcome data. Studies are classified by strategy components. Risk of bias is assessed with design-appropriate short tools, and certainty is rated per outcome with GRADE.

outcomes.name: Low-value testing
outcomes.measure: Change in the proportion of patients receiving at least one low-value test, or tests per patient, as reported, by strategy type
outcomes.why: The outcome the committee must act on.

outcomes.name: Durability
outcomes.measure: Effect at the latest follow-up of 12 months or more, by strategy type
outcomes.why: Education faded within a year elsewhere; the committee needs lasting change.

outcomes.name: Same-day cancellations
outcomes.measure: Proportion of procedures cancelled on the day, before and after the strategy
outcomes.why: The committee's main concern about stopping tests.

outcomes.name: Perioperative complications
outcomes.measure: Complications or unplanned admissions within 30 days, as reported
outcomes.why: Stopping tests must not cause harm.

outcomes.name: Evidence base per strategy
outcomes.measure: Number and design of included studies, and certainty rating, per strategy type
outcomes.why: Shows where the committee's choice rests on thin evidence.

feasibility: About 1,500 records expected; single screening with verification fits two analysts at one day a week each over eight weeks, with the librarian's two days a week for searching.
biasMitigation: Verification of 20 percent of screening decisions and all full-text exclusions
Second-analyst checking of all outcome data
Certainty per outcome with GRADE, stated in plain terms for the committee
Limitations of rapid methods reported explicitly

biasFlags.label: Missed studies from single screening
biasFlags.note: Verification sample estimates the miss rate.

biasFlags.label: Weak designs in included studies
biasFlags.note: Most are before-after; certainty ratings carry this.

biasFlags.label: Language restriction
biasFlags.note: Stated as a limitation; unlikely to change the strategy ranking.

flags: Two balancing outcomes carry the committee's safety concern
parsimony.simplestPath: One primary outcome by strategy type, one durability measure, two balancing outcomes, narrative synthesis.

theoreticalFramework: None imposed; strategies are classified by component so that the committee can see which levers were used.
summary: Rapid review with one primary outcome by strategy, a durability measure, two balancing outcomes and a process measure of the evidence base.
